newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures end mixed on spread action.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures end mixed on spread action.

text.p: CME lumber futures closed mixed with bear spreading combining with concern over sluggish cash lumber sales to take January sharply lower in an expanded $15.00 per thousand board feet trading limit, traders said.
Lumber closed off $8.80 to up $2.00 per tbf with January off most at $380.70 and March off $1.90 at $375.30 per tbf.

Spreads look for March to eliminate its discount to January, especially with the current weak tone to cash markets and expected better demand for wood by next spring. January is not the best time to build and demand for wood rises going into the spring, traders said.
The Canadian quota, if there is any effect from it at all, will likely have more effect on the March contract, they said.

Cash sources noted that spruce prices continue to slip in slow trade. Mills are asking $390 to $400 per tbf but the secondary market is actually trading somewhere between $375 and $390. Random Lengths should quote spruce prices lower on Friday's official price, they said.
